utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated, we can resume our hearing now. Registrar, would you have the accused brought in, please. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do the interpreters hear me? Is everybody ready? Good morning. Does everybody hear me? The Defence, Prosecution, Mr. Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLASKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour, I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. So we can begin. It was Mr. Gregory Kehoe representing the Office of the Prosecutor to continue with the questioning of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, good morning Mr. President, your Honours. As the Prosecutor's next witness, the Prosecutor would like to call Cazim Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness, the Tribunal and judges would like for you to go as quickly and directly to those basic questions for the Prosecution, and that we attempt not to get into too many details, because that opens out the possibility of an even longer cross-examination than it might have been, and then because you have a purpose by bringing in this or other witnesses, and the Tribunal would like to get as quickly as possible to the heart of the matter. Of course, we are not going to control the questions you ask, that is not the purpose that we are seeking, but we want you to go directly to the essential part of your questioning, as the Defence should also do when its turn comes. The witness's name is what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Cazim Ahmic, C-A-Z-I-M.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: About how long have you planned for this morning with this witness? (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have allocated two and a half, your Honour, but I believe I will be done more quickly than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you hear me? Could you tell us your last name and your first name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ahmic Cazim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cazim Ahmic, you are going to read, while you are standing, the declaration which the usher is going to give you which is the oath. Go ahead. Read the document, please. CAZIM AHMIC (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. You may now be seated. You were called by the Prosecutor as a witness for the Prosecution as part of the trial which is being conducted in this International Criminal Tribunal against General Blaskic, who is in this courtroom. You are a Prosecution witness and the Prosecutor will therefore ask you a series of questions, as you know, and afterwards the Defence, defending General Blaskic, will, like in all courts, then ask another set of questions. But for the time being, please relax, you are sitting before judges, you have nothing to fear. Try to answer as clearly as you can the questions that Mr. Kehoe the Prosecutor will ask you. Mr. Kehoe, go ahead, please. Examined by MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Ahmic. Mr. Ahmic, how old are you and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Pirici, the municipality of Vitez. I am 55 years old, I was born in 1941.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, prior to 16th April 1993, did you live in the village of Zume?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zume was a village that was sometimes connected to Santici and sometimes connected to Ahmici and sometimes connected to Pirici, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were living there, you were working at the Vitezit factory, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vitezit, excuse me. Prior to 16th April 1993, you had spent your whole life living in the Pirici and Zume area, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me about your family on 16th April 1993, and I am talking about your immediate family, wife and children. Did you have a wife and did you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had a wife and children. My wife was killed, my son, my mother, my sister, a nephew. That was my next of kin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a daughter as well who survived, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, the troubles in the Ahmici area began on approximately 20th October 1992, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about what happened, tell the judges what happened on the morning of 20th October 1992, when you and your family were in your homes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, around 5.30 or 5.40, in front of the house of Semren, our neighbours, a gun, a cannon fired the mosque in Ahmici. That is how it started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continue on. What did you see throughout that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the mosque was fired at, from the house of Jozo Covic and Mirica Selenka, they are my first neighbours, my house was shot at from these houses by Semren Dario, Mario, actually, Ivica, Covic Jozo, Zoran Covic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these men Croats or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croats, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any other shooting go on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was shooting, there was shooting elsewhere, but I cannot identify exactly who shot at who. I saw these people shooting at my house, but there was shooting in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this shooting take you by surprise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, of course it would surprise you if somebody shoots at your house. Ivica Vidovic, from his house, my house was also being shot at. I was surprised, of course I was surprised, naturally a man is surprised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this shooting started, what did you and your family do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We immediately sought shelter so that no one would be hit. A barn was already burning down there, so we did not want someone to be hit. Normally we sought shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to a thicket down there below my house, along the road, towards the road below my house. That is where we were hiding until the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the evening, as it was getting dark, we moved up towards Ahmici, towards Gornji Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what did you do up there, sir, and how long did you stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came there in the evening and we did not spend much time there, we went to Vrhovine, where it was safer, Vrhovine, further up above Stari Ahmici, so it was further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay there for a period of time before returning to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We stayed up there for about five or six days, about a week, but I cannot tell you exactly how many days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen that caused you to return to your house? Was there an agreement, some type of peace agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some kind of agreement must have been made most probably as soon as we were called to go back to our homes. Probably there was some kind of agreement reached among the people down there, so we all returned home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, on the morning of 20th October, did you see any artillery pieces on trucks or artillery pieces from the surrounding area firing into Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the judges what you saw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Donje Rovine, from that direction, from Donje Rovine, a vehicle came from that road on to the main road, I do not know, it was some kind of heavy weapon. It was shooting as it drove along, in two places roughly, in Ahmici and Gornji Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about from the area of Hrasno. Was there any artillery shooting into Ahmici from Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was a mobile vehicle, but also from Hrasno, from the Rusici houses and from Hrasno, artillery was shooting from there in the direction of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission may I approach and have the witness stand up, and I believe we are going to talk about 50E, which is the pre-marked map which is on the easel. If I can ask you to stand, Mr. Ahmici, and use this microphone -- let me see if it is on. Just stand right there. Mr. Ahmic, just looking at this map of 50E, which is a map of the Ahmici, Zume, Pirici, Santici area, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to where your house is in Zume?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My house in Zume is here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is marked with the number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to get our bearings here, on this photograph, Ahmici is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, if you want to come closer to the map, because they were pre-marked lines on it before, so in order to avoid any questions you might ask, I would like you to come close to the map to make sure what the Prosecutor is putting on the map matches what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We looked at it before the hearing, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interests of moving this matter along, working with the witness, we pre-marked this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that was a very good initiative, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, point to the area of Ahmici. You just pointed to Zume, so where is Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ahmici is over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Santici is over here (indicates), already 25th May that is where Santici is. I am sorry, perhaps somebody cannot hear me, that is why I keep repeating this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right now, the area of Zume is connected to Santici, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. That is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the morning of the 20th, you were in your house and you said that the firing came from over your house toward the mosque. Where did that firing come from? Could you point to that on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Semren's house and the shooting came from in front of his house and they were shooting towards the mosque, up here towards the mosque. This is where the mosque is roughly, so it was in front of this house, this is Semren's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is marked on the exhibit as number 2, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they hit the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they hit the top of the minaret.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: For clarity of the record, the witness is not indicated the point at which number 2, the arrow, is directed. He indicated a location immediately to the right of the block containing number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is why I wanted you to be near the map so you would not have to ask these questions later. I did not grant an objection of yours the other day, I do remember, but I would like us to move forward, so Mr. Kehoe, is the witness showing it clearly? I have trouble seeing from here and it is not very clear on the monitor either. Mr. Kehoe, is he indicating where it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The number 2 is pointing to Semren's house and the firing was coming in front of Semren's house into the mosque, but the number 2 is pointing actually to Semren's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is just a matter of making sure that when the witness points to a location, the record actually reflects what he is identifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Okay. If we could repeat this so that it is in the transcript -- all right, let us go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you said that in addition to the firing into the mosque from in front of Semren's house, there was additional firing going on on a house close to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the house of Jozo Covic and Milica Selenka, over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am showing the number, I am showing the house directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From that house of Jozo Covic and Mirica Selenka and Ivica Vidovic, called Jevcen, from behind his house, from this area, my house was shot at. They shot at my house from rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that a truck with a heavy weapon came down from Rovine and came to the road and was firing into Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the road (indicates). That is the road. They were shooting from this area when the vehicle just got on to the main road and then it moved lower, and then it was shooting up towards Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other location that you mentioned, which is not on this map, is the area of Hrasno, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hrasno, these are the Rusici houses up here, and Hrasno is up here, that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was another location that was firing into Ahmici, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, artillery. I am not very good at this, I am not very knowledgeable as far as these arms are concerned, I do not know exactly which is which.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, if you could please be seated again and I will go back to the podium and we can continue the questions. Mr. Ahmic, prior to this shooting into your house on the morning of 20th October 1992, and the firing on to the mosque, did you have anything to do with any roadblock that took place on the Vitez Busovaca road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have anything to do with it. I imagine there was some kind of roadblock near the catholic cemetery down there, but this was not in my village, I had only heard about it, that there was a roadblock there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you even see the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see it, I did not go down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a civilian, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, after this incident, the attack on 20th October 1992, did the HVO collect weapons from Muslims in your village and in surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and some of the people who had guns handed them over, people from the area of Zume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hand your weapon over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no weapons, I had a hunting gun and why would I hand that over?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we move ahead into the area of April 1993, Mr. President, your Honours, I would like to move into evidence Prosecutor's exhibit 50E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No objection. I do not think all the numbered locations have been identified, but we have no objection as to what has been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The four locations that were listed up there were number 1, his house; number 2, Semren's house that fired on to the mosque; number 3, another house in the area that fired into his house; and number 4, the area that is on the road where the truck came down from Donje Rovine and fired into Ahmici. All four areas have been indicated and identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe is not the witness. The record is what it is, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, I think this was marked in the transcript. Mr. Hayman, that has to do with the identification. I would like us to go on, we can put this into the record.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be 50E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, continue please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we move into the area surrounding 16th April 1993, we would like to move to an exhibit that was introduced into evidence yesterday, which is I believe 56D, and with the assistance of Mr. Dubuisson or the usher, that is the next exhibit that is underneath this particular copy and if we could just flip it over, we could ask a question or two about that exhibit before we move into April 1993. If I could approach, Mr. President? Mr. Ahmic, if I could ask you to stand once again with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, you said you lived in this area your entire life, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just back away, are you familiar with a petrol station on the Vitez bypass road that had a bear in a cage next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the petrol station of Kreco Asim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Kreco Asim? Is he a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim, a Muslim, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to it on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it. (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the area circled there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over here, over the bridge the hunting lodge is there and then the petrol station of Asim Kreco.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ahmici. You can take a seat, please. Mr. Ahmic, let us move ahead to the area, the time surrounding 16th April 1993, the morning of the attack. Prior to the attack on 16th April 1993, did you know that you were going to be attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not know. Had we known, we would have got out and tried to save ourselves. We did not know anything that we would be attacked, at least not my village, and I did not know anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was home at your house that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who spent the night at the house, in the house, who was there, I mean my family?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, your family.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was my wife, my son, my daughter, a nephew of mine, Brkic, Enver Brkic from Busovaca. He was spending that particular night at my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything unusual happening that night in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not notice anything unusual happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That evening, had you got a phone call from your neighbour, Senada? We are talking about the evening of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Senada. I cannot remember her last name because she moved in there later on. She called me in the evening and she said that she was standing in front of her house before that and that Ivo Vidovic came in front of her house with two unknown men, and said "you are not supposed to go anywhere, it is night-time, you are not supposed to go anywhere", so what were his intentions? No one knew. That is why she called me. That was probably a HVO patrol. She called me and she asked, "what is this all about?" I said, "I have no idea. Are there any other signs? I do not know anything". So that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of night was that phone call, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10.30, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, let us move to the morning of 16th April 1993. Can you tell the judges what happened on the morning of 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 16th April 1993 in the morning, early in the morning, about 5.30, a shell hit my house. It came through the window. It was of a smaller calibre, so that I jumped up to see what was happening, where it had come from, and it was -- it came from Anto Covic's house, because Jozo Covic came out, rubbing his hands, saying "I did a good job". Jozo Covic, Anto Covic's son had fired that shell. It was of a smaller calibre, probably. Then the real shooting started all over the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what you did, Mr. Ahmic. You said the real shooting started; even before we get to that, if I may, when you looked out and saw Jozo Covic rubbing his hands as if he had a good shot --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assumed he was pleased with the effect he had produced. Of course, we immediately started to look for shelter where we should go. I looked through the window and I saw that it was an out and out attack, and that we had no choice but to withdraw towards Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, in your area of Zume and Santici, there were both Croat houses and Muslim houses, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a mixed village or settlement. As far as I was able to observe, because it is a flat area, every Croatian catholic house nearby was marked, because from every chimney stack there was smoke coming out and probably this was a sign marking the house. That is my assumption, because there was no smoke coming out of Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, there was smoke coming out of the Croat houses and no smoke at that time in the morning coming out of the Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw the attack begin. Was it Muslim houses that were being attacked or Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim houses, Muslim, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you looked out the window and you saw this attack taking place, tell us what you saw. Tell the judges what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What was happening was an attack on this settlement. My house was hit by this shell from Jozo Covic's house, people were running, they were calling Pezer Sefik, so there was all out shooting everywhere. They called his name, they cursed him, they insulted him, they called him to come out, cursing his "balija" mother, saying if he did not come out, they would burn down everything. There is some glass on his staircase, and I saw a soldier from behind climbing up the steps and there was smoke already, so I realised what was happening, but this all took place at lightning speed, so I realised it was a general attack, so immediately we started running away towards Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, the person that you are talking about whose house they were calling to, who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sefik Pezer, Pezer Sefik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the soldiers in his house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw one soldier climbing up the steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What army was that soldier from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see any insignia, because it is not so close, but knowing that my house had been hit and that they were cursing the "balija" mothers, one knows what army it was, the HVO army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to Sefik Pezer and his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was killed, as well as his son. Sefik Pezer was killed and his son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near your house and Sefik Pezer's house, did Ibrahim Pezer live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did, Ibrahim Pezer and Sakib Pezer. They killed Sakib then as well, and his son, and Ibrahim and his wife and Besim and his wife and son, they killed them all, they were killed then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they also set Ibrahim Pezer's house on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see that at that time. I could not see that, as far as Ibrahim Pezer's house is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, if you could move a little bit back from the microphone, it would help the interpreters. You are a little bit too close to the microphone. Thank you very much. Continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, you said that you were in the house that morning with your wife and daughter, and your son and your nephew. Where did everybody go when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We ran from the house in the direction of Ahmici. As I was the last to leave the house, when I got to Esad Ahmic's house, meaning I had crossed the street, by that time already, no one knew where everyone else was. I did not know where my son was, my wife, my daughter, my nephew, and then I continued towards Ahmici. One of the -- Esad Ahmic was in the courtyard in front of his house and I was behind his barn, and one of the soldiers reached his yard. I could not see, but I assume it was a pistol, I heard a shot, I later heard his wife calling him out "run, run, the children have left". He probably did not want to run from his own yard, he said, "I am not going anywhere". So that a soldier reached him, a shot could be heard and then she started screaming, and I hear this man saying, "run, go", and then she ran out into the road next to me. She had caught sight of me, and she said, "run, at least so that you remain alive. They are killing everyone". So from there we went on together towards Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, you said that Esad Ahmic's wife was screaming. Was she screaming after she heard the shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She said something to the effect, "why are you killing him? Why have you killed him?" Something to that effect, "why, why are you killing him?" It was already clear what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Esad Ahmic have a family as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a family, and when we got there, just below Vlatko Kupreskic's house, we were somehow crawling up towards this house of Vlatko Kupreskic, I and Esad's wife found my wife, who was seriously wounded in the head. Esad's daughter Hajra was dead, and his other daughter, Besima, she was also wounded in the leg. So we stayed there for a while. I do not know exactly for how long, three or four hours. It was in a kind of ravine, and we waited there for our fate, we did not know where we should go or what we should do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, Esad Ahmic had two daughters that were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three daughters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Three daughters, and two of those three daughters were present on the morning of the 16th, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all present over there, but one got killed, one was wounded. But they were present, his wife too, and his little son, Islam, together with my wife, my daughter. Then there was Senada there, there was Osmancevic Zulejha there, they are all neighbours who ran away and we caught up with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Esad's daughter Hajra was killed when you got up to the area around Vlatko Kupreskic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I got there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Besima, his daughter, was wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was wounded in the leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that your wife was wounded in the head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the head, very seriously wounded. She still gave signs of life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was she wounded, where was the gunshot wound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave her first aid, from the back of the head, and I assumed the bullet came out above the left eye, above the left eyebrow, and her eye had started coming out already. She was hit in the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, how many people were with you in the ravine for that three to four hour period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Esad's wife, three daughters, the little boy, myself, my daughter, then Senada, I cannot recall her surname, and Zulejha Osmancevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilians, of course, all of them. They were women, girls, children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now there were other people, civilians, that were killed up near you that you could not see their bodies, Fata Pezer and Dzana Pezer, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pezer, her father-in-law, Aziz. I could not see that, I learnt about that afterwards. She was not far, maybe 30 metres from me. There is a slight slope there so I could not see it, and then they said that apparently Fata had been killed, but I could not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Fata Pezer a Muslim and a civilian also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was a sick woman, she had bad kidneys. She was a civilian, of course, a woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all these people that were up there in the ravine with you, were they all Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All Muslims, yes, all of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you went up to a ravine by Vlatko Kupreskic. Who was Vlatko Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vlatko Kupreskic is the son of Franjo Kupreskic, a neighbour, one might say. He worked in the SPS. I do not know much more about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The SPS factory is in the same location as where you were, the Vitezit, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I worked in Vitezit. It is in the same location. It used to be one factory and then it was divided into different departments, as we called them, basic organisations, and then they became work organisations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was going on when you were in the ravine, did you see or hear what was happening at Vlatko Kupreskic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see anything, because it is again in a downhill, in a kind of hole. Then there is a path and we could see people running across that path to and fro all the time. They kept crossing this path. There was shooting coming from all directions all over the place. Then afterwards, I do not know exactly how long we were lying there, three or four hours, and then suddenly someone in front of Vlatko's house said, "gather together". He said "it is over. We have finished our work", so that a group of HVO soldiers, five of them, across the way from Zlatko Kupreskic, there is a small thicket and they were coming out of that thicket, these five men, when they called them out, and they noticed us in this ravine, and they immediately said, "how come you are there? What are you balijas doing there?" So they searched us immediately. They found on Senada 300 or 400 marks, Deutschmarks in her handbag. They took it away. They did not find anything else on the others, on me and the others. Then they lined them up in a row, in a line, and since my wife was on the ground lying down and I was next to her, one of them came up to us, saying that he was going to cut our throats, both of us. He was cursing our balija mothers, saying, "what are you doing alive on this land?" Then they were taking a decision as to whether they should shoot us or slit our throats, and then one of them said, "you know, I am from Nezirovic. Do you know where that is?" I said, "I have no idea". "Do you know where Kacuni is?" "Kacuni is near Busovaca". He said, "I am from Nezirovic and I am going to cut your throats, both of you", and he took out a knife. Then one of them, young men, one of these young men, said, "wait a minute, let us see what we should do with them, whether we are going to shoot them or not", so they were consulting amongst themselves as to what they should do. The decision was taken why they were wearing masks so I could not recognise any of them, they may not have been from our parts, they were wearing masks, so I have no idea. They decided not to liquidate us. They said, "get lost". One of them came up to me, asked me where I was from, and said, "why are you not over there where your people are? Why are you here?" I said, "I do not know who mine are or where they are. I would not be coming here if I knew" and from Ivica Kupreskic's house there was a lot of firing in the direction of the school, towards Donje Ahmici, and then he said, "why are you not over there?" What he meant, I do not know. "I have no idea", I said, "this is not where I am from, I am 500 metres away from here". So I said "I started running away with these women and children, you see my wife is half dead" and he said, "run as fast as you can and get away from here, because no Muslim may tread this earth. If any other group would have come along and found you, they would have executed you without any qualms. You are very lucky it was us who came across you. Go and run for your life. No Muslim may stay here. If they learn that I let you go, I will be executed", he said. So that I asked Kupreskic, he had come out to see what was happening, and I asked him for something, a wheelbarrow or something, so that I could get out towards Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which Kupreskic was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Franjo Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was an older man, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, an older man, the father of Vlatko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we talk about your conversation with Franjo Kupreskic, the HVO soldier that told you to leave, that you were going to be killed if you were met by any other HVO patrol, did he appear to be the leader of that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume he could have been, because he had that small, what do you call it, radio station, a walkie-talkie, some kind of earpiece. He was holding it in his hand, so I assume he could have been the leader because he was the one who told us the decision that we would be allowed to go free and to go towards Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he had a walkie-talkie or a Motorola in his hand to talk to other people with, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was moving away, he did not speak to anyone in front of me when they were consulting amongst themselves as to what they should do, he would move away from us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, you said that you went to Kupreskic Franjo and asked him for some help. Tell the judges about that, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as Franjo came out of the house to see what was happening, whether he knew in advance or not, I do not know, and I asked him if he could give me something, a cart or something, and he said "I do not have anything like that". "Then give me an axe at least, so that I can make some kind of a carrier, something for my wife". I had to get to Ahmici and there is quite a sharp slope, so that I could get my wife up there, because she was still alive. He did not give me anything. One of the soldiers told him, "give the man an axe or something", and then he gave me a blunt axe, upon the insistence of this HVO soldier, so I cut off two pieces of wood, and using the clothes and the sleeves of a piece of clothing, we managed to carry my wife, I and my daughter and Senada, and Osmancevic, and we managed to carry her up to Ahmici. When we got there, UNPROFOR, two armoured vehicles of UNPROFOR arrived. They came something a little before 1.00 in the afternoon, about 12.30, about 1.00, somewhere around there, and they extended first aid to my wife, and they took her off to Travnik. Probably she underwent surgery. She was not saved, she died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did your wife die and where was she buried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She died at the hospital in Travnik and she is buried in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you identify your wife and how did you know that she died in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know because she was carried away by the UNPROFOR to Travnik, and when it was possible to go to Travnik across the hills, I went there, and I enquired at the hospital, and in the morgue, because she did not have any ID documents on her. But a picture of her was taken after her death, and under a code number and the picture I identified her, so that I know it was my wife. She was buried on 24th April, and she was hit on 16th April and buried on the 24th, under the number of 03, but that does not matter anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, your wife was buried in Travnik. Were other Muslim civilians that were killed in the Ahmici, Zume, Santici area, were they buried in places other than in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some at Poculica, and others who were burnt down in that house in Ahmici, also in Poculica and in Stari Vitez, also in Travnik you see, and there are some people about whom no one knows where they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, after UNPROFOR took your wife to Travnik, what did you do and what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know what, I did not know about the rest of my family, and there was a lot of shooting going on in Ahmici, I was already up there in Ahmici, so I could not move until night fell, and I would not dare either. So then during the night I moved up there, it was -- all of Ahmici, everybody had fled, Ahmici was empty, everyone went to Vrhovine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were fleeing towards Ahmici, you are talking about upper Ahmici, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, upper Ahmici, Gornji Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the area of upper Ahmici, Gornji Ahmici, did you see fire, artillery fire and shooting coming from areas surrounding Gornji Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was shooting all over, artillery was hitting Gornji Ahmici too from the Rusici houses and from Hrasno, just like on the 20th, from Mete, from Borik. You can see Ahmici well, and these special bullets, fragmentation ammunition was used and then there is this area called Borik in Mete and smaller ammunition was used from there, fragmentation ammunition and then from Hrasno and also from the Rusici and Mijanvic houses, that is that area, Donje Rovine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So artillery fire was coming from Hrasno and Donje Rovine, the same locations that were used on 20th October 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And on the 20th, yes, on the 20th too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ultimately escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all escaped from Ahmici, from upper Ahmici. No one was out there. Whoever had survived left, and during the night everyone moved towards Vrhovine. Some people went to Zenica. Everybody fled. I was waiting in Rovine, I did not know what had happened. I did not know that my mother was killed, I did not know that my sister was killed, I did not know about my son, I did not know that day about my son, about my nephew and my mother, what had happened to them, so I was waiting up there in Vrhovine so that some of them would come if they had survived, but then as other people came I found out that they were all killed. I did not know immediately that all of them were killed, all my people were killed, so that is why I stayed in Vrhovine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission, if we could move to the next exhibit which is the map 50F, which is again a pre-marked exhibit, your Honours, of the Ahmici, Pirici, Santici area. If I can approach the witness? Again Mr. President, if I could ask Mr. Ahmic to stand up by the microphone with his pointer, we have a series of locations on the map to point out to your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ahmic, you have understood what the Prosecutor has asked. Are you all right, Mr. Ahmic? Do you want to take a break now? We are going to have a break soon anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not get a translation. That will be fine if your Honour wants to take a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will have a break soon, but I was really asking Mr. Ahmic whether he felt all right, whether he wanted to take a break now and resume at 11.30, or, Mr. Kehoe, if you have a few more questions about this particular exhibit, we could also have a break in five or ten minutes. Mr. Ahmic, how do you feel? These memories are very painful for you and the Tribunal is sensitive to that fact. We are going to ask you certain things about the map -- are you all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely, that is what I wish to say. But whatever you prefer, whatever you decide, because these are painful memories for me, repeating this tragedy is -- but you do your job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, perhaps you could ask one or two more questions and then we will stop. All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, again, if we could stand up to the map that has been identified as 50F. Just for the record, Mr. President, this is the same exact map as 50E, but we just have different numbers, one being the 20th October period, this being the 16th April 1993 period. Again, taking a look at this map, Mr. Ahmic, your house is again listed or marked as number 1, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my house. (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That has the number 1 marked on it, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is marked with number 1. This is my house. I do not look at the numbers, you know, I look at the place. This is my house, this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This number 2, this particular house here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the house of Anto Covic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the house where the firing into your house was coming from early in the morning on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind the house of Anto Covic there is a shed, and Jozo shot at my house from that shed on 16th April. I saw him when I got up. That is where the firing came from, because my window faces Anto's house directly, so I saw Jozo when he got out, and I saw him rubbing his hands like this (indicates), Jozo Covic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next house right here, which has the number 3, whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Sefik Pezer, this is Sefik Pezer's house and this is Mustafa Pezer, called Ibrahim, this is his house. But number 3 is Sefik Pezer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 4 is Ibrahim or Mustafa Pezer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mustafa Pezer, but his nickname, his another name is Ibrahim. He was killed, his wife and his son Fadil, this is his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sefik Pezer and his son were killed as well in number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were killed too, and next to him is the house of his uncle, Sefik Pezer, he was killed as well and his son too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sefik Pezer, house number 3, is the house where you saw the soldier going up the staircase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are glass windows near the staircase, so I saw the soldier walking up happily, they were not calling out Sefik's name any more because they were calling out his name and they were cursing his balija mother and they were saying "get out, get out, otherwise we are going to set you on fire", so I had assumed that he and his son were killed and I saw the back of this soldier going upstairs and then I saw the smoke that started coming out. That meant that he had set the place on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think this is an appropriate time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will resume in about 20 minutes, around 11.35. It will be 11.35, 20 minutes. (11.15 am) (A short break) (11.35 am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is now resumed. Please have the accused brought in. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, do you hear me? Have you rested up a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have rested and I feel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, then we can resume, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, your Honours, thank you. If I could just go back to the map again and resume where we left off just before the break, and if I could again ask Mr. Ahmic to stand up by the microphone with the pointer. Mr. Ahmic, you said that you left your house and headed in the direction of Esad's house. Can you point to that direction? Just using the pointer, can you show us the direction that you went in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my house (indicates), and I left the house and started going in this direction, this is the house of Esad Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Esad Ahmic is the house that has the number 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, number 5, that is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the house where you heard Esad Ahmic's wife saying, "why are you killing him?" And then her telling you "leave, they are killing everybody"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was behind the barn, this is my barn, and there is a shrub there, by the road, this is where I hid, so the army, the HVO army already came into the yard. A small shot rang out, probably somebody shot a pistol, I imagine, and she was saying, "why are you killing him?", and this and that, and somebody told her, "get lost! What are you saying?" She went out on the road, so we were running away together and she said, "run, run, they are killing everyone. You should at least try to stay alive", so we were withdrawing along this road gradually over here (indicates). We had difficulty in crossing the road here, because from here, from the house of Ivica Kupreskic, there was shooting coming from that house. I do not know what they had, a machine gun or something, maybe it was a machine gun, I do not know, but they were shooting at the school and at the mosque, and when they would stop a little, then we would cross to the other side. There was a ravine down here, near Vlatko's house. It has all been flattened out now but that is where we hid and that is where we found my wife. Esad's three daughters and his young son Islam, my wife and my daughter were there and Zulejha Osmancevic, and Senada. I cannot remember her last name because she came from elsewhere. So we were hiding there below Vlatko's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The place where Ivo Kupreskic -- the machine gun was firing from Ivo Kupreskic's house, that is marked with the number 8, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, number 8, that is the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The place that you went to in the ravine, that is marked with number 6, where your wife was lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 7 is Vlatko Kupreskic's house, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Vlatko Kupreskic. After you were released by the five HVO soldiers, you said you took your wife up towards Gornji Ahmici. Can you show us the direction you went in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From here along this road up there, that is where I went (indicates). This is Matif Dzamir, the matif mosque of upper Ahmici. I took the road leading to the area up here. That is where I arrived with my wife, my daughter was there, Zulejha Osmancevic and Senada, Esad's wife parted from us and her two daughters and her little son was there too, but one of her daughters was killed, was back there and she went towards Pirici, along this path.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The area, the place where you and your wife went to in Gornji Ahmici is marked with number 9, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it. I already indicated that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am just clarifying the number, Mr. Ahmic. Is that approximately where the UNPROFOR vehicle picked up your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they came along this road, the same road that I took to Ahmici, and as they were coming I walked towards them and I gave them signs, I tried to show that there were wounded people there and they probably had an interpreter with them anyway, and they said that they would turn around and they came here, to the intersection, and they went back and they gave first aid to my wife. They took her and I asked them to take her to Zenica and they said, "only to Travnik, that is as far as we can go", and they took her to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Esad's wife took this road down towards Pirici that you just pointed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, towards Pirici. Up here, above Vlatko's house, there is a separate path that goes to Pirici (indicates). She took that path so she parted with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She passed the house where your mother and your sister lived, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they went this way and this is the house of my late mother and sister. I heard from her that she saw both of them killed in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your mother and sister's house is marked with number 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I will offer into evidence Prosecutor's exhibit 50F, which is this map. (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, 50F, Registrar. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with Mr. Dubuisson's assistance, I would like to move to the next exhibit, which is 53A, which is again underneath this exhibit. 53A has no markings on it. It is a map that has previously been received into evidence as Prosecutor's exhibit 53 and it is a wider angle view of the Ahmici area. Mr. Ahmic, you said previously in your testimony that there was artillery fire coming from the area of Rovine and Hrasno. Could you use this particular --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Donje Rovine, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, if you could use this particular marker and mark the areas in Donje Rovine and Hrasno where the artillery fire was coming from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the path from Donje Rovine that leads to the main road, through Lasva, across Lasva and here, this is the Rusici houses, on this location. That is where the fire was coming from, hitting Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you circle it so we could see it, sir? It might be a little difficult to see with that marker, but could you circle the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map). This region here, this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, he might want to try a different colour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Donje Rovine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, if you could use this colour so the judges can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, no problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You also mentioned another artillery fire location as Hrasno. Could you also circle that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we have to unfold the map more. It is off the map. Hrasno -- perhaps you will not be able to see it, it is here, roughly here, from this location here, roughly. (Indicates). I cannot see it very well -- now that is better, that is better. It is from this area of Hrasno that Ahmici was fired at with artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you make that circle --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both on 20th October 1992 and on 16th April, I was in Ahmici and artillery fire was coming from Hrasno and from Donje Rovine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, can I ask you to make that area a little darker so the judges can see it? That area of Hrasno, could you mark it a little darker with the marker in your hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course I can. This is this area, Hrasno. This is Donje Rovine. All of this is Donje Rovine, this part here, but roughly the fire was coming from here, the artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there also fire coming from areas that were just outside of Gornji Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand. I do not understand the question. What did you say? I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you were hiding in the bushes on the evening of the 16th, was there also fire coming from the area -- into Gornji Ahmici from an area just outside of Gornji Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell exactly, I do not know about that exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, you can have a seat, sir. Your Honour, at this time the Prosecutor will offer 53A into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: May I just ask, please, where is Vitez on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is not on this map. Mr. President, if I could now move --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could now move to a series of photographs that have been marked already as exhibit 108, and if I could request the assistance of the usher and the ELMO for a series of photographs to be placed on the ELMO. (Handed). If you could take them out of the binder and just take them one by one. Mr. Ahmic, the first photograph, which is 108/1, do you recognise those two men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, it is Sefik Pezer and his son Ahmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those the two men who were killed on the morning of 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were killed in the morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next photograph, 108/2. Do you recognise that man and that woman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Pezer Mustafa, known as Ibrahim, and his wife, Cazima.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they also killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were also killed on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 108/3, the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Ibrahim's son, Adil. He was killed too on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 108/4, the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the family of Esad Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you use the pointer, with the assistance of the usher, could you use the pointer on to the photograph, Mr. Ahmic. You have to point it on the ELMO. Can you point out Esad Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Esad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he killed that morning as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was killed. I was behind his table when he was killed, just behind his table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also saw one of his daughters shot and one of his daughters wounded that morning as well, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is his daughter Hajra, whom we found dead up there and this is Besima, the little one. She was wounded in the leg, just below Vlatko's house. They cannot hear me if I do not speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let us turn to the next photograph and I believe it is 108/5: you mentioned a woman by the name of Pezer Fata that you could not see but was also killed in the area. Do you know who this is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Fata Pezer. When I reached this group of women and children, she was on a slight -- there was a small slope between this ravine and she was lying dead on the other side of this slope. That is what they told us when we got there, they asked me, "did you see Fata? She is here" and I said, "no, I did not see her". They told me she was just around the corner, so to speak, and that is this Fata.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But she died that morning as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go to the next photograph, 108/6. Do you recognise anybody in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my son, Besim who was killed, who was killed on that day. This one. (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This photograph, Mr. Ahmic, was taken in happier times, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were his school mates from his school, they were in fourth grade of the chemical school in Vitez. They were his friends from his class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those friends include Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know only this one, he is Ahmic Sulejman. I know the others from sight. This one is a Croat. There were Croats there too. This one is a Croat. (Indicates). Most of these here are Croats. It was a mixed class, it was normal in those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your son died that day as well, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I learnt that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go to the next photograph. I believe it is 108/7. Do you know that young man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my nephew, Brkic Enver, who disappeared on that day too. He was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the nephew that was living in your house on the morning of 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is the one, Brkic Enver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next photograph, 108/8?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my sister, Ahmic Zulejha.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next photograph, 108/9?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My mother, Hajra Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, were your sister and your mother together when they were killed on the morning of 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They lived together, and I heard from the one who escaped, Ahmic Azra, I learnt that she had seen them at the doorstep of their home, both of them killed, shot down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecutor will offer into evidence Prosecutor's exhibit 108. Mr. Ahmic, your wife, your son, your nephew, your mother and your sister were all killed that day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the family name of Ahmic, you had many cousins living in that area, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, we are all more or less related, roughly. There were about 50 relatives of mine who were killed on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you lost 50 members of your family on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecutor has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, the questions that the Prosecutor asked you to answer which bring such painful memories to you are now completed. This is a trial against a man who has been accused and who is presumed innocent. He has two defenders, and now it is General Blaskic's lawyers' turn to ask you questions. You are under our protection and you can speak without fear and you may answer as best you can the questions that one of the two Defence counsel will ask you, either Mr. Nobilo or Mr. Hayman -- Mr. Nobilo, then, who is one of General Blaskic's defenders, who is now going to ask you a series of questions. If you have any problem at all, do not hesitate to ask, to interrupt and I will speak with my colleagues and we will try to make sure that everything goes as best as it can for you. Mr. Nobilo, it is now your turn. Cross-examined by MR. NOBILO

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Ahmic, good morning, as the President has told you, my name is Anto Nobilo, I am Defence counsel for General Blaskic and I only have a few questions on behalf of the Defence and I hope we will not keep you long. On the eve of 16th April 1993, you mentioned several of your neighbours. What were the relationships between the Croats and the Muslims prior to that date? Were they the same as they used to be a couple of years before then, or had anything changed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course it had changed. It was changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe what those relations were like, how they had changed among what used to be good neighbours, Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the 16th, before this unfortunate event, the weeks and months running up to April 1993; for instance, with your next door neighbours, Croats, did you have good relations, did you say hello to each other, or was there tension between you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in very good relations with them. I do not know what the reason could have been to attack me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after October 1992, the neighbour who fired at your house, did you ask him, "why did you shoot at my house?" Did you talk about that at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What could I ask him? There is nothing to ask. How could I say "why did you shoot at me?" What is there to ask?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say hello to one another after that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In most cases, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Kupreskic family that you mentioned, what kind of relations did you have with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had very good relations with them, especially with the older Kupreskic, Franjo. As far as I am concerned, I personally -- when we met, we would exchange greetings and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us to explain why you think those neighbours that you mentioned, Kupreskic and your next door neighbour, Jozo and the others, what happened? Why did they act in that way? Can you know why it happened, can you explain it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you, I see no cause, no reason at all for them to attack me, to kill my wife, to kill my mother, to shoot at me. What was the cause? I am not a politician, so I do not know why or how this happened, what was the reason for all of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you are not a politician; were you elected into the Presidency of the branch of the Party of Democratic Action of Ahmici on 16th September 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Together with Ahmic Ejub, Ahmic Rasim, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any other Cazim Ahmics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my name is Ahmic Cazim Besim and there is Ahmic Cazim Jahim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The roadblock from October 1992, how long was it there for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Believe me, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the roadblock was in Ahmici, right, on the road next to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lower down, on the main road, at least that is what I heard, near the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then why did you run towards Ahmici if something was happening there, and the reason for the conflict was in Ahmici? Why did you flee towards Ahmici and not in some other direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean Ahmici? Gornji Ahmici and the road down under it, there is a big distance between the two, there is a large distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be really very brief, let us go to the 16th. I know this is very difficult and painful for you, but just a little patience. On the 16th in the morning, when the shell fell in, was your son up already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all jumped to our feet, because every piece of glass -- pieces of glass were all over the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your son have a weapon in his hand on that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your son a member of the TO or the BH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a weapon in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your nephew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not have any weapons on him either, at the time, on that day, at home, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that a box of anti-tank mines, anti-infantry mines and another box of anti-infantry mines, two automatic rifles and a hunting rifle were found in your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of it. It was not there. What they could have said ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that your son, when he was hit, was in a group with the following young men: Enver Brkic, Muharem Djidjic, Nedzad Djidjic, Budo Osmancevic, Ibrahim Karic and his son Ibrica, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible because that is what I heard from Ivica, that they had been together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all conscripts, soldiers, these men that I have listed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, if you remember; your late son, which unit did he belong to of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a signals man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Attached to which unit? Where was the command of the unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prevocica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Prevocica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have listed a number of names of people who you saw killed or dead. Could you say whether you saw any one of these persons actually being wounded and in what way they were wounded? You saw that they were wounded, but how, who had fired, from what distance? Did you see any of those things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see that exactly, who had hit whom. I saw who fired the shell at my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see that. I could hear the cries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we try to focus on the time Vlatko Kupreskic said, "the job has been done".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who said it, but it was in front of his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me when this happened in time, roughly? I know it is very difficult for you to locate that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only say very roughly how much time I spent there, about three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, around noon, 12.30, somewhere around that, around 12.00. I did not look at my watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, but let us try and locate this more precisely. At what time did you encounter the UNPROFOR vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was already up there in Ahmici and the UNPROFOR could have arrived somewhere just before 1.00. I had only just reached there and UNPROFOR came after me, so it must have been before 1.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So UNPROFOR was there before 1.00, around 1.00. So if we go back in time, how much time before UNPROFOR did somebody say, "the job is done, it is over" in front of the Kupreskic house? Could you tell us whether that was half an hour, an hour, two hours before the arrival of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been about one hour before then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if UNPROFOR came around 1.00, then this statement was heard around 12.00, or before 12.00. Tell me, when you were lying next to the Kupreskic house could firing still be heard the three hours you spent there? Was the fighting very intensive or was it more sporadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was occasional fire, but I could not pay any attention. I had found my wife there, there were dead people there, I could not really think about anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, but when the soldier came up who was not a neighbour, this group of soldiers who asked you why you were not at the front --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, "why are you not with your own people", and I said "how do I know where mine are and who are mine?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say that they were in the school or in the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assumed and he mentioned, he said, "why are you not over there", down there where the fire is directed against the mosque and the school, from Ivica's house, at least that is what the soldier said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you looking towards the mosque and the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How could I look?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Vrhovine, when you escaped from this whole situation, was life there normal or were the inhabitants abandoning Vrhovine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The inhabitants did not leave Vrhovine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a mixed village, Bosnian Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is just Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Vrhovine is a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am almost done. Could you list the neighbours that you saw engaged in combat operations, fighting with arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 16th April, I saw only Jozo Covic, who fired at my house. Judging by the hole in the wall, it must have been some kind of hand grenade or something, a lighter calibre weapon. There was running across the path from Sefik Pezer's house and others, but there were HVO soldiers running around, but I could not identify any individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of your neighbours did you see under arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 16th? I have just told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you add up all the soldiers you saw, how many did you see? How many HVO soldiers did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Without any identification, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just how many persons you saw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not count them, man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But roughly, roughly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Kupreskic's house, there were five of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
