utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was for a time -- he participated in the distribution or assignment of these patrols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say that he was commander for the whole of Ahmici for a certain period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What role in the army did your neighbour Fuad Brbic have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fuad Brbic in my opinion, he kept track of, how shall I put it, of the people who assigned these patrols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was superior to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in my opinion he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me summarise: Fuad Brbic was superior to those people who would assign you to patrols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a mobilisation, which means it was not just voluntary service but that young men were mobilised into the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Hazrudin Bilic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Hazrudin Bilic was actually one of the people in charge of these patrols, and he assigned people to the patrols for night duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mirsad Bilic a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not really know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you remember tell me, if you do not just say you cannot remember. Would you see him in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirsad Ahmic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his role?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my view, his role was the same as that of this Bilic, to assign people to the patrols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Fuad Brbic with some kind of a radio communicating with Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a radio was it, can you describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. It was a radio, about 50, 60 cent metres high, with an antenna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told me that he had communicated with Vitez. Do you know with who in particular in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea. I know that this radio station was at the school for a time, and I too, in the absence of others, was assigned to be on duty at the school with another friend of mine, and a third person who operated the station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the radio station was at the school. What was the school, was it some kind of a headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I do not know myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who came to the school where the radio was when you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was on duty, no one came except the person on duty with me, Hussein Ahmic, and this third person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the radio in the school, did you see anything stored there, any military material stored there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, 100 per cent no. Absolutely nothing. People were absolutely unarmed, there was the radio station and that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rasim Ahmic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rasim Ahmic? Yes, I know him. He lived below the road at Zume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he too a member of the TO military units and on watch duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But to go back to the school where you kept -- were on duty, can you remember when this was? Was it in 1993 or in 1992 or both years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was some time between -- in the autumn of 1992, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Rasim came from the Donje Kuce lower houses. Do you know Hazim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, he is his brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I know that he worked as a cobbler.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Nazif Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him very well, there are three brothers that you have asked me about, these two, and this one is the third.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ejub Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ejub Ahmic? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is from Pirici, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zijad Bilic and Dramo Bilic; do you know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nazif, the third brother, Nazif, was he in the TO army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You asked me about Nazif; Nazif, Rasim and Asim, they are three brothers, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, I forgot. Do you perhaps remember October 1992, there was some shooting and a clash over the roadblock at Donje Ahmici, near the main road and the catholic cemetery; do you remember that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not know anything about that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anything. In 1992?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, 1992 October.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, your son Zikret, he was in the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what his position was, what his rank was? He was an educated man, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not know where he was working, what unit he belonged to and what place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this conflict, did he stay on in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more thing. Your son left Vitez, where did he go, to Mahala or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he came to Zenica, thank you. I am not going to torture you once again, so that you will not have to describe the crime committed against your family, but I am just trying to ask you to remember the time when it happened, around what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to April 16th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, when your family was murdered. When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was exactly in the morning at 5.30, at 5.30 am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know Hazim Ahmic who built the Donje Jahmir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have some kind of private army in the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The previous day, did you perhaps see a white Lada car with foreign people coming to Hazim, to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you near the mosque then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not even know where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 16th April 1993, when you were in the barn, what time was that, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The time -- I cannot remember the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw this heavy machine gun or semi-automatic rifle shooting from the Kupreskic house towards Donje Jahmir, the mosque, can you remember that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard it, I heard the shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard the sound but you did not see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see it with my eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the area around the new mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cannot see that area, I did not see it, you could not see it from the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you recall when you saw the UN tanks, what time that was approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that time either. I cannot remember the right time, you know, at those moments, given everything that was going on and everything that was happening to me and my children and my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course I appreciate that. You said the tanks, they were white. Were those the tanks that have a gun or those that do not have a gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did have a gun in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Big gun? Did it have a machine gun or a cannon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had a machine gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was not a tank, it was an armoured vehicle with a gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An armoured vehicle with a gun, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have regular rollers, wheels or caterpillars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Caterpillars, yes, they were the same, both tanks in front of Ivica Kupreskic's house and from front of my house, they were the same, the two tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described some time ago that you reached Baringi and you felt 100 per cent safe. Can you tell me why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because everything in the area of Ahmici and Zume, everything was burned down and everybody was killed. The HVO army killed everyone. So when I came to my mother's house, they had not reached Pirici yet, the HVO, they were below Pirici, but at that moment, they came to Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, but why did you think that Baringi was safe? I understand your life was jeopardised near Ahmici, Pirici, Zume et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I saw that everything was intact up there, no one was up there. That was why I felt 100 per cent safe. I was sure that no one was up there everything that was done was happening in the area of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at Baringi, did you see the BH-Army setting up positions there to defend you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see the positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There was not a living soul up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Jozo Covic burned down your mother's house with another man. Where is he from? Where did he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is Jozo Covic's son, I do not know his first name. He lived in Zume, down there, and my mother told me that when they came to her place, she said, "it is Ana's son, Nikola's grandson from Zume".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him, you knew his father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know them very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we say he is a neighbour of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We lived about 700 or 800 metres apart, from one house to the other there was 700 or 800 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ahmic. Mr. President, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Again, turning to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I then turn to my colleagues to ask whether they have any questions they would like to ask, perhaps Judge Riad has a few. The judges will ask you a few additional questions, and then your testimony will be complete. Judge Riad will first ask you a few questions. Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Sakib Ahmic, you mentioned that you had a truck in front of your house and in front of another house, and then this truck left, whether it is a truck or a tank, and shooting started, and I can mention your words, you said the shooting was so strong that the ground, the earth was moving, was shaking. If there was so much shooting, what were they shooting at, because previously you mentioned that the Armija military had no presence in Ahmici. So what was the HVO shooting at with such strength?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The truck that the gentleman is asking me about, I never said that there was a truck in front of my house. I just said that I saw a little truck, yellow, on the 13th or the 14th in the evening, around 9.00 in the evening. It came in front of the house of Ivica Kupreskic. That is number one. Number two: I heard shooting in front of the house of Ivica Kupreskic. I think that they were shooting towards the mosque in Donje Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was destroyed in the mosque, the minaret or -- what were they shooting at, at the mosque? What did they want to destroy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment, I do not know. I do not know what they wanted to destroy at that moment, but at any rate, it was obvious later that the mosque was totally ruined, and that the minaret was broken and it had fallen down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other mosques around the area or in ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they also shot at and destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those mosques were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that when Smail Pezer and Sulejman Pezer got out and hid in a small canyon, they were shot at and then HVO soldiers reached to them and searched their bodies. Does that mean that HVO soldiers were around during these killings, and were they doing the killing, or just watching?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, let me just repeat the question the way I understood it. Is the question related to the death of the four or five young men near Vlatko Kupreskic's house? Is that the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you a more general question. Most of the killing was done by private people or by HVO, or by people linked with the HVO like Zoran, if I understand rightly, Zoran Kupreskic, whom you said was dressed in black and had a radio, so how was the killing done, by whom, in general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was done by the HVO army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to ask you a very general question. You said that you lived very happily, when you started speaking to us, you lived very happily with your Croatian neighbours. When was this turning point where everything went wrong, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, there were no turning points. I think that until the very last moments we had good neighbourly relations, and we never doubted these neighbours of ours. We were always good and true neighbours. We never could have thought of something like this happening, let alone having it actually happen. I mean all of that that happened on 16th April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Shahbuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHBUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, you saw Zoran Kupreskic in a black uniform on the morning of 16th April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him in my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the first time you had seen him in a black uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw in a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him in a black uniform before that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you identify that black uniform, as belonging to what military group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That black uniform belonged to HOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So he was a HOS member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you explain --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion, judging by his uniform, the black uniform in which I saw him before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then explain why is it that you were referring to HVO people being around? Was he a HVO member also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may say so, I can say that everything that was done in the territory of Ahmici was done by the HVO army, and on the day of 16th April, Zoran Kupreskic, who wore a black uniform, to my home, I really do not know why he did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know to what organisation he previously belonged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion -- actually I do not know if I can really answer this question, whether he really belonged to the HOS or whether he belonged to the HVO army. When all of this happened on 16th April, at that time HOS did not exist. As far as I knew, HOS was integrated into the HVO army, so it was a single HVO army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Like Mr. Nobilo, I do not want to torture you with questions relating to the details of certain parts of your narrative, so let me ask you a question about Ljuba Vidovic, who I think took in your mother. She was a Croat person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other Croats who rescued other Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally, on the territory of Ahmici, I have not heard until the present day about any one of these Croat neighbours trying to rescue any Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So any rescue of that kind would have taken place outside of Ahmici, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we are talking about my mother -- is that what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is precisely what happened. It happened outside Ahmici, because that area belongs to the area of Santici, where my mother was rescued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. One last question about relations between Croats and Muslims. You said that before 16th April, relations between those two bodies of people were good, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally still have friends amongst the Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you one or two questions about that yellow truck. Was that the first time that you ever saw that yellow truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the first time I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that also the last time that you saw it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First and the last time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have a covered back, or was the back an open back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An open back, a small TAM truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did it leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It came in the evening, around 9.00 pm, but it was customary, in the case of my neighbours, the Kupreskics, to have an external light on in front of my house too, and Vlatko's, and Zoran's, and the Bilic, and everywhere else, but that night, when the TAM truck arrived, approximately around 9.00 in the evening, not a single light was on outside any one of the Kupreskic houses. The truck parked by Ivica's house and I saw it around 7.00 in the morning as it drove out of Ivica's yard by Zoran Kupreskic's house. It honked its horn and moved on to the Sarajevo Travnik main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know. At what time did you observe that the back was an open back, when it came or when it left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that it was open in the evening when it arrived and also in the morning as it was leaving and when I say that I saw that it was in the evening too, what I am saying is as it was entering Ivica Kupreskic's yard Ivica's father's house had lights on at one window, at another window, so as the truck drove into Ivica's yard, I saw because of the lights from Ivica's father's house that it was open at the back and in the morning when it was leaving Ivica's house, I saw that it was open in the back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHBUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, I believe that Judge Riad still has another question he would like to ask. Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just ask, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic, please try to give me a clear answer to a statement you made to the Defence attorney, Mr. Nobilo. You mentioned to him that you ran away because the HVO, and I am quoting your words, "killed everyone". Does that mean that there was a general extermination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They killed everyone who they came across. For example, there are some survivors who are women, children, but most people were killed, and all Muslim houses were also burned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The testimony is now complete, Mr. Ahmic. This was a long day for you. Do you have the feeling that you have said everything that you had to say to the Tribunal? Do you wish to add anything? If not, the testimony is complete.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may, I wish to thank the entire office of this court, and I want to thank everyone for the honest and fair way I have been treated and the way in which I have been asked questions. I thank the entire court over here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, we can now have Mr. Ahmic accompanied out of the courtroom, and we can wish him only calm and serenity for the rest of his life after these dreadful events. Then we will ask the Prosecutor to introduce the following witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On my part, I wish all these people the very best, the people that I have been seeing over these past two or three days here in The Hague, in the state of the Netherlands, thank you all very much. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, our next witness will be Elvir Ahmic. We are not prepared to proceed with him at this point in time and would request that we proceed with him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Because the witness is not here, is that why?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, he recently arrived, he is here in the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, we then agree that we will begin tomorrow morning at 10.00. In the future, if possible, Mr. Harmon, try to be sure that there is not too much time lost this way, time which we could have perhaps used for the testimony. But we will now adjourn our hearing and begin tomorrow again at 10.00. (5.30 pm) (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day) 24 25
